newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE new crop wheat falls to lows on strong stg.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE new crop wheat falls to lows on strong stg.

text.p: LIFFE grains ended down in thin volume with the strength of sterling sending the traded new crop months on wheat to contract lows, traders said.
November was the most active contract on wheat, with 162 of a total 309 lots. It last traded 0.25 stg down at 83.00 stg, a contract low.
The biggest fall was for front month July. It last traded 1.00 stg lower at 78.00 stg, on volume of 29 lots.
Barley also fell. Active November last traded 0.75 stg lower at 78.75 stg on 73 of a total 121 lots on barley.

Market players were holding back ahead of a predicted rise in interest rates, one trader said. "People are keeping their powder dry," he said. A big rise in rates could send sterling up and hit the grains market again. Too small a rise could bring the currency down and give a short term boost futures, he said.
The market was still fundamentally weak, with a big crop expected. "That's getting a bit boring now. We'd like to see the crop come in," he said.
